parts.title: Shipwreck In The Forbidden Zone
parts.article:
A On 7 March 1533, a fleet of large Portuguese trading ships left Lisbon and sailed down the River Tagus towards the Atlantic Ocean. Their destination was India, and the return journey was expected to take approximately fifteen months. The ships hoped to bring back valuable spices, particularly pepper, from Portugal’s expanding network of overseas trading ports. Among the vessels was the Bom Jesus, or "Good Jesus", a recently built ship owned by King João III. It was commanded by Dom Francisco de Noronha and carried around 300 sailors, soldiers, merchants, priests, nobles and enslaved people.

B The Bom Jesus never reached India, and for almost five centuries its fate remained uncertain. Investigating the loss was especially difficult because most of Portugal’s official maritime records had been destroyed in 1755. In that year, a powerful earthquake struck Lisbon and was followed by a tsunami and fire. The Casa da India, where maps, sailing charts and records of voyages had been stored, collapsed into the river. Consequently, historians attempting to identify lost Portuguese vessels have had to depend on scattered documents and archaeological evidence.

C One important clue came from the gold coins discovered in the wreck. A large number were Portuguese coins produced during the reign of King João III between 1525 and 1538. As these coins were later withdrawn and melted down, their presence helped researchers establish a relatively narrow date for the voyage. The cargo also included an enormous quantity of copper. Such metal was normally carried from Europe to India, where it could be exchanged for spices. This showed that the ship was probably travelling towards Asia rather than returning to Portugal. Researchers then examined the surviving narratives of Portuguese fleets. These documents listed 21 ships that had disappeared while sailing to India between 1525 and 1600. Of these, only the Bom Jesus, which left Portugal in 1533, was reported missing anywhere near Namibia. A surviving illustration from the 16th-century Memória das Armadas provided further evidence. It showed a ship from the 1533 fleet sinking beneath the waves and identified it with the single word perdido -- lost.

D Although no complete account of the disaster survives, researchers have reconstructed a likely sequence of events. Approximately four months after leaving Portugal, the fleet encountered a violent storm near the Cape of Good Hope, and its ships became separated. The damaged Bom Jesus may then have been caught by the strong winds and currents running along the south-western African coast. These forces probably carried it hundreds of kilometres north before it struck rocks close to the Namib Desert. Part of the stern broke apart, and heavy copper ingots fell through the damaged hull as the ship sank.

E The wreck was finally discovered in April 2008, not by professional archaeologists but by workers at a diamond mine near the town of Oranjemund. Mining companies in this region construct enormous barriers to hold back the Atlantic Ocean and then remove the seawater so that diamonds can be extracted from the exposed seabed. During one such operation, a machine operator uncovered copper ingots and elephant tusks. Further investigation revealed timbers, cannons, swords, muskets, navigation equipment and thousands of coins. The mining company immediately stopped work around the site and invited specialists to conduct an emergency excavation. The location offered unusual protection from treasure hunters because it lay inside one of the world’s most closely guarded mining areas, formerly known as the Sperrgebiet, or "forbidden zone". Archaeologists described the discovery as exceptionally important, since very few Portuguese ships from this period had ever been scientifically excavated.

F Ironically, the copper that had contributed to the ship’s loss also helped preserve it. The ingots weighed down sections of the vessel and prevented them from being carried away by waves and storms. In addition, the presence of copper discouraged some marine organisms that would normally have consumed the wood. Archaeologists carefully measured and photographed the surviving structure and used three-dimensional scanning equipment to record the site. The remains rested below sea level, behind the temporary wall created by the mining operation. Maintaining a dry excavation area was both difficult and expensive, so the team had limited time to recover and document the objects before the ocean was allowed to return.

G The fate of the people aboard remains a mystery. A small number of human bones were found beneath the ship’s timbers, indicating that at least one person died during the wreck. However, these were the only human remains at the site, and relatively few personal possessions were discovered. Some archaeologists therefore believe that many of the passengers and crew may have reached land. Survival would nevertheless have been extremely difficult. The surrounding desert was cold in winter, almost uninhabited and far from normal shipping routes. No rescue party knew where to search for the missing vessel. However, the Orange River lay a short distance south of the wreck and could have provided fresh water. Shellfish, seabird eggs and desert snails were also available as food. Local hunter-gatherers sometimes travelled through the region during winter. Archaeologists have suggested that the Europeans might have survived if they met these groups and traded peacefully with them, although no historical record confirms that such an encounter occurred.

H There is a final irony in the story. The people aboard the Bom Jesus had left Europe in search of wealth, yet they were shipwrecked on one of the richest diamond-producing coastlines in the world. For millions of years, diamonds had travelled down the Orange River from deposits far inland. After reaching the Atlantic, the stones were carried north and deposited along the desert coast. The same cold current that transported this extraordinary wealth may also have helped drive the Bom Jesus towards its destruction.

Questions 1-7
Complete the notes below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
The Final Voyage of the Bom Jesus
• The ship departed from in March 1533.
• The fleet intended to obtain pepper and other from Asia.
• Gold helped researchers establish the approximate date of the wreck.
• The presence of large amounts of indicated that the ship was travelling towards India.
• Surviving records showed that the Bom Jesus was the only vessel of the period lost near .
The Discovery and Possible Survival of the Crew
• The remains were uncovered during work at a mine.
• People who reached land may have obtained fresh from the Orange River.
Questions 8-13
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write:

Q8 The Bom Jesus was owned by a group of private Portuguese traders.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q9 Researchers identified the wreck by consulting the complete records formerly kept in the Casa da India.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q10 A surviving report written by the fleet commander provides a detailed account of how the ship sank.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q11 The cargo of copper contributed to the preservation of parts of the vessel.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q12 The survivors used pieces of the damaged ship to construct shelters in the desert.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q13 An ocean current associated with the movement of diamonds may also have influenced the route taken by the damaged ship.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

解析 原文明确提到1533年3月这支船队从Lisbon（里斯本）出发。

干扰 你可能想选Portugal，但原文指出具体出发的港口城市是Lisbon，填空题通常需要填最精准的地点。

句子 A On 7 March 1533, a fleet of large Portuguese trading ships left Lisbon and sailed down the River Tagus towards the Atlantic Ocean.

Q2

解析 原文提到船队希望带回珍贵的spices（香料），特别是题目中提到的pepper（胡椒）。

干扰 你可能因为看到India而想填India，但题目问的是和胡椒并列获取的物品，对应原文的spices。

句子 Their destination was India, and the return journey was expected to take approximately fifteen months. The ships hoped to bring back valuable spices, particularly pepper, from Portugal’s expanding network of overseas trading ports.

Q3

解析 原文表明，沉船中发现的金币（gold coins）帮助研究人员确定了航行的具体时间范围。

干扰 你可能会忽略题目中的Gold，填成clue，但这里需要填的是具体的物品coins来和前面的Gold构成合理搭配。

句子 One important clue came from the gold coins discovered in the wreck. A large number were Portuguese coins produced during the reign of King João III between 1525 and 1538. As these coins were later withdrawn and melted down, their presence helped researchers establish a relatively narrow date for the voyage.

Q4

解析 原文指出，大量的copper（铜）通常被运往印度，这表明船只是驶向亚洲的。

干扰 你可能会想填metal，但metal在原文中是个代词，指代的是前一句明确提到的具体物质copper。

句子 The cargo also included an enormous quantity of copper. Such metal was normally carried from Europe to India, where it could be exchanged for spices. This showed that the ship was probably travelling towards Asia rather than returning to Portugal.

Q5

解析 原文清楚写明，在遗留的记录中只有Bom Jesus号是在Namibia（纳米比亚）附近报告失踪的。

干扰 你可能看到Portugal就想填，但Portugal是船的出发地，题目问的是这艘船在哪里附近失踪。

句子 Researchers then examined the surviving narratives of Portuguese fleets. These documents listed 21 ships that had disappeared while sailing to India between 1525 and 1600. Of these, only the Bom Jesus, which left Portugal in 1533, was reported missing anywhere near Namibia.

Q6

解析 原文明确说明，这艘船的残骸是被一个diamond（钻石）矿的工人们发现的。

干扰 你可能会填Oranjemund，但题目空在mine（矿）前面，需要填的是矿的种类diamond。

句子 The wreck was finally discovered in April 2008, not by professional archaeologists but by workers at a diamond mine near the town of Oranjemund.

Q7

解析 原文指出，沉船南边不远处的奥兰治河（Orange River）可以提供新鲜的water（水）。

干扰 你可能会根据荒野求生的常识脑补填food，但原文明确指出Orange River能提供的是fresh water。

句子 However, the Orange River lay a short distance south of the wreck and could have provided fresh water.

Q8

解析 原文明确表示这艘船的主人是国王若昂三世（King João III），而不是私人商人。

干扰 你可能看到第一句的trading ships就误以为是私人商人的船，但做题必须定位到针对Bom Jesus号具体所有者的描述。

句子 Among the vessels was the Bom Jesus, or "Good Jesus", a recently built ship owned by King João III. It was commanded by Dom Francisco de Noronha and carried around 300 sailors, soldiers, merchants, priests, nobles and enslaved people.

Q9

解析 原文指出Casa da India里的完整航海记录已经在1755年的地震中倒塌掉进河里毁坏了，研究人员只能依靠零散的文献。

干扰 你可能只在原文扫到了Casa da India这个词就匆忙判断，没有往后读到这些记录早已被毁（destroyed/collapsed）的事实。

句子 Investigating the loss was especially difficult because most of Portugal’s official maritime records had been destroyed in 1755. In that year, a powerful earthquake struck Lisbon and was followed by a tsunami and fire. The Casa da India, where maps, sailing charts and records of voyages had been stored, collapsed into the river. Consequently, historians attempting to identify lost Portuguese vessels have had to depend on scattered documents and archaeological evidence.

Q10

解析 原文一开头就明确说明“没有关于这场灾难的完整记录留存下来”，直接推翻了题目中“有详细记录”的说法。

干扰 你可能会因为后面详细列出了沉船的过程而认为是舰队指挥官写的，但那其实是研究人员推测重建（reconstructed）出来的。

句子 Although no complete account of the disaster survives, researchers have reconstructed a likely sequence of events. Approximately four months after leaving Portugal, the fleet encountered a violent storm near the Cape of Good Hope, and its ships became separated.

Q11

解析 原文直接点明，导致沉船的铜同样帮助保存（preserve）了这艘船的某些部分。

干扰 你可能会根据常识觉得铜那么重只会砸坏船体，但紧接着的原文解释了铜压住船体并驱赶了破坏木头的海洋生物。

句子 Ironically, the copper that had contributed to the ship’s loss also helped preserve it. The ingots weighed down sections of the vessel and prevented them from being carried away by waves and storms. In addition, the presence of copper discouraged some marine organisms that would normally have consumed the wood.

Q12

解析 原文只提到幸存者可能到达了陆地，以及沙漠的生存条件恶劣，完全没有提及他们是否用破损的船体残骸建造了避难所。

干扰 你可能会根据“沙漠里冬天很冷”加上人类求生本能脑补他们建了避难所，但雅思阅读必须严格依据原文，没说就是NOT GIVEN。

句子 Some archaeologists therefore believe that many of the passengers and crew may have reached land. Survival would nevertheless have been extremely difficult. The surrounding desert was cold in winter, almost uninhabited and far from normal shipping routes.

Q13

解析 原文指出，运送钻石财富的同一股寒流（cold current），可能也推动了Bom Jesus号走向毁灭，即影响了它的路线。

干扰 你可能因为句子比较长，没看懂this extraordinary wealth其实指代的就是前文顺流而下的钻石，从而错失了洋流和船只路线的联系。

句子 For millions of years, diamonds had travelled down the Orange River from deposits far inland. After reaching the Atlantic, the stones were carried north and deposited along the desert coast. The same cold current that transported this extraordinary wealth may also have helped drive the Bom Jesus towards its destruction.
